question: Under what exact learning and support assumptions does compositional generalization force vision embeddings to decompose into additive concept factors with orthogonal cross-concept differences, and do pretrained encoders exhibit the predicted geometry?

key_findings.claim: The paper's necessity theorem is an exact conditional result for binary concept grids, linear heads, gradient descent on separable cross-entropy, and stability across every valid training support; it is not a general theorem that ordinary held-out compositional accuracy requires orthogonal representations.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 1 assumes Divisibility, Transferability, and equality of calibrated posteriors after retraining on any two valid supports. Its two support families are either every subset of size 2^(k-1)+1 or an anchor plus all k one-coordinate flips. The conclusion is an additive representation z_c=sum_i u_i,c_i with orthogonal differences between distinct concepts. The authors explicitly call Stability an idealization and leave approximate stability for future work.

key_findings.claim: Within its stated model, Proposition 1 derives linear factorization and cross-concept orthogonality, while Proposition 2 gives a dimension lower bound d >= k independent of values per factor.
key_findings.evidence: The binary result represents each of the 2^k grid points as a sum of 2k value vectors and makes each concept-flip direction perpendicular to every other concept's flip direction. Divisibility of the linear decision arrangement then needs at least one independent direction per concept. The paper also supplies a binary sufficiency result under the same GD-plus-cross-entropy and support conditions, but the multi-valued extension is constructive rather than the same necessity theorem.

key_findings.claim: A domain mismatch in the proof leaves the affine-parameter identification step unjustified unless the realized embeddings affinely span the representation space or Stability is strengthened beyond its definition.
key_findings.evidence: Desideratum 3 equates posteriors only for x in X, hence at points in f(X). Lemma 1 assumes equality for every z in R^d and uses z=0 plus arbitrary z to conclude that both weights and biases are identical. Equality on a finite grid instead identifies an affine function only on its affine hull; no full-affine-span assumption or quotient-space reformulation is stated.

anchors.section: Appendix B, use of Lemma 1 in Lemma 3

key_findings.claim: The proof presented for the more-than-half support regime switches to cross-datasets that are not members of that regime, so the first branch of Proposition 1 lacks a demonstrated bridge.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix B states that the default valid support has size 2^(k-1)+1 but that the proof works with cross-datasets of size k+1. For k beyond the smallest cases, those cross-datasets do not satisfy the default cardinality rule. The proof then invokes Stability across valid cross-datasets under either regime without constructing allowable supersets or showing that the learned maximum-margin separator is preserved when the extra points are added.

anchors.section: Appendix B, opening proof setup and Definition 6

key_findings.claim: The optimization argument conflates the asymptotic direction selected by cross-entropy gradient descent with a finite calibrated posterior model.
key_findings.evidence: On separable data, unregularized logistic-loss weights diverge while their direction approaches a hard-margin SVM solution. The proof treats finite SVM-scaled weights and biases as the output of GD and simultaneously requires exact equality of sigmoid posteriors across retrainings. Directional convergence alone does not identify scale, bias, or calibrated probabilities, and no stopping rule, normalization, regularizer, or limiting-posterior definition repairs this mismatch.

anchors.section: Appendix C.1, SVM interpretation of GD plus CE

key_findings.claim: Pretrained encoders show partial additive structure and checkpoint-level association with held-out probe accuracy, but the measurement is correlational and partly couples the representation score to the evaluated concepts and labels.
key_findings.evidence: Across CLIP, OpenCLIP, MetaCLIP, SigLIP, and DINO checkpoints on PUG-Animal, dSprites, and MPI3D, projected whitened R-squared is above a random-encoder baseline and rises with held-out linear-probe accuracy. Factor vectors are marginal means, and R-squared is computed after projection onto the learned probe span and PCA whitening. Those operations use the same concept ontology and dataset embeddings as the probe task; no rotation, factor intervention, or representation-edit experiment establishes that linearity or orthogonality causes the accuracy.

key_findings.claim: The empirical protocol does not test the theorem's exact Stability premise and has split, tuning, seed, and contamination limitations that prevent a scale-general causal conclusion.
key_findings.evidence: The main text says probes train on 10% and evaluate on a held-out 10%, whereas Appendix H.1 defines held-out fractions including 0.90 and trains on the remaining 10%; the intended main split can be inferred but the wording is inconsistent. Probes run 1,000 epochs and the best of two learning rates is reported without a separate validation rule. Main checkpoint correlations lack uncertainty; three seeds appear only in robustness appendices. Pretrained encoders may have seen the named concepts and combinations, and the synthetic study directly optimizes one embedding per combination for 50,000 epochs rather than training an encoder. The paper itself says that synthetic result is not a guarantee of generalization.

anchors.section: Appendix H.1, split sweep and probe optimization
Appendix H.7, synthetic protocol and qualification

method.core_idea: Formalize compositional generalization as divisibility, transferability, and retraining stability of linear concept readouts, derive geometry forced by those properties in a binary grid under GD-plus-cross-entropy, then measure approximate additive and orthogonal factor structure in frozen pretrained vision embeddings.
method.mechanism: For the theorem, concept classifiers trained on carefully specified supports are identified with maximum-margin separators. Exact stability is used to equate separators across supports; paired cross-datasets make single-coordinate flips support vectors, yielding context-invariant flip directions and cross-concept orthogonality. Empirically, concept-value factors are estimated by marginal embedding averages, embeddings are projected onto the probe span and PCA-whitened, additive reconstruction R-squared and cosine similarities are calculated, and linear probes are evaluated on held-out combinations.
assumptions: The concept space is a fully crossed Cartesian product with one representative embedding z_c per concept tuple and no within-cell nuisance variation in the theorem.
The main necessity result is binary-valued even though most empirical datasets are multi-valued.
Readouts are affine and are trained by unregularized gradient descent on separable binary cross-entropy.
Every allowed support satisfies perfect transfer to the full grid and exact equality of per-concept posterior probabilities after retraining.
Either all supports with more than half the binary grid or all anchor-and-one-flip cross supports are considered valid.
Posterior equality on realized inputs is treated as sufficient to identify affine parameters throughout R^d.
Asymptotic max-margin direction is treated as an actual finite classifier with stable probability scale.
Marginal means, probe-span projection, and whitening recover concept geometry without making the metric circular or transductive.

techniques.role: Defines divisibility, full-grid transferability, and posterior stability across retrained supports.
Uses anchor-plus-single-flip supports and hard-margin support-vector geometry in the necessity proof.
Estimates each concept-value vector by averaging embeddings over tuples sharing that value.
Measures additive reconstruction after projection to the probe span and PCA whitening.
Compares absolute cosine similarity within and across concept-factor direction sets.
Trains one frozen-encoder linear classifier per concept on sampled combinations and tests other combinations.
Optimizes a free vector per synthetic tuple under CE/BCE and Euclidean/spherical geometry.

evaluations.setting: Frozen OpenAI CLIP, OpenCLIP, MetaCLIP/2, SigLIP/2, and DINO v1-v3 encoders on PUG-Animal (39,168 samples), colored dSprites (180,000), and MPI3D-real-complex (64,800).
evaluations.metric: Projected PCA-whitened additive R-squared and factor cosine geometry.
evaluations.result: Across checkpoints, projected whitened R-squared is about 0.40-0.60 versus 0.12-0.42 for the random encoder. Mean absolute factor cosine is about 0.53-0.55 within concepts and 0.09-0.12 across concepts, versus 0.32 across concepts for the random encoder; these are descriptive comparisons across heterogeneous checkpoints.
evaluations.baseline: A randomly initialized OpenCLIP ViT-L/14. Model families differ by architecture, dimension, parameter count, objective, data, and compute, so checkpoint comparisons do not isolate geometry.

evaluations.setting: One linear probe per concept, trained with Adam for 1,000 epochs and the better of learning rates {1e-3, 1e-2}; Appendix H.1 sweeps held-out fractions {0.95, 0.90, 0.50, 0.30, 0.10}, and H.5.1 sweeps 13 train fractions from 0.001 through 0.999 over three seeds.
evaluations.metric: Mean per-concept classification accuracy paired with projected R-squared.
evaluations.result: Higher projected R-squared is visually associated with higher mean per-concept held-out accuracy in every plotted dataset/split panel, including the full 32x32 dSprites position grid; the paper reports no correlation coefficients, controlled regressions, or main-panel confidence intervals, so the evidence is qualitative checkpoint association rather than an effect estimate.
evaluations.baseline: Random encoder and lower-R-squared pretrained checkpoints; the same target concept labels inform both probe span and factor metric.

evaluations.setting: Zero-shot text probes on PUG-Animal and the sparse ImageNet-AO subset of 3,243 images spanning the 80 most common nouns and 80 most common adjectives.
evaluations.metric: Zero-shot concept accuracy, additive-factor R-squared, and cross-factor cosine structure.
evaluations.result: Appendix figures report qualitatively similar R-squared/accuracy associations. On ImageNet-AO, CLIP ViT-L/14 mean absolute cosine is 0.10 noun-noun, 0.14 adjective-adjective, and 0.07 cross-concept, while the random baseline is about 0.49 both within and across; this supports prompt-readout robustness but not exposure control.
evaluations.baseline: Alternative checkpoints and prompt names; no contamination audit or encoder trained on a verified zero-combination support.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic concept grids with k up to 10, n in {2,6,12,24,48,96}, dimensions 3-32, CE versus BCE, and Euclidean versus spherical embeddings.
evaluations.metric: Additive R-squared, within/cross-concept absolute cosine, and minimum dimension attaining at least 0.99 per-concept accuracy.
evaluations.result: Most cells reach R-squared at least 0.7; cross-concept cosines tend to shrink with k; CE in Euclidean space often approaches d approximately k while BCE often needs about 2k and spherical geometry adds roughly one dimension.
evaluations.baseline: Loss/geometry cells optimize the tuple embeddings and probes jointly for 50,000 epochs on all or up to 100,000 sampled combinations; there is no encoder, unseen-combination evaluation, or compute-matched representation intervention.

evaluations.metric: Seeds, split construction, tuning protocol, exposure control, and architecture matching.
evaluations.result: Three-seed checks are confined to appendix robustness plots, main correlations have no error bars, the best of two probe learning rates is selected without a stated validation set, and pretrained data exposure is unmeasured. Scale spans 21.6M-3.6B frozen encoders but not controlled training-scale interventions.
evaluations.baseline: No support-retraining stability experiment, verified pretraining holdout, matched architecture/compute sequence, or factor-edit causal control.

limitations: Author-stated scope, reviewer implication: Stability is an exact worst-case idealization across every valid retraining, making the headline 'requires' much stronger than ordinary high held-out compositional accuracy.
Author-stated scope: the necessity theorem is binary and assigns one embedding per concept tuple; the empirical datasets are multi-valued and contain nuisance variation.
Reviewer-identified proof gap: Lemma 1 requires equality over all R^d although Stability supplies equality only on f(X); an affine-span condition is missing.
Reviewer-identified proof gap: the more-than-half validity proof uses smaller cross-datasets that are not valid under that family without establishing an extension argument.

Reviewer-identified optimization mismatch: unregularized separable cross-entropy converges only in direction while weights diverge, which is incompatible with finite calibrated-posterior equality as written.
Reviewer-identified measurement coupling: projected whitened R-squared depends on the learned probe span and known concept labels, tying the explanatory metric to the downstream task.
Reviewer-identified null concern: marginal centering, whitening, and high ambient dimension can make unrelated directions look nearly orthogonal.
Reviewer-identified exposure gap: pretrained encoders are not trained on verified factorial holdouts, and benchmark concept/combination exposure is not audited.
Reviewer-identified protocol contradiction: split language differs between the main text and Appendix H.1, and learning-rate selection lacks a separate validation criterion.
Reviewer-identified statistical limitation: main checkpoint comparisons omit seed uncertainty and statistical tests while conflating architecture, objective, data, dimension, and scale.

Author-stated scope, reviewer implication: the synthetic appendix directly optimizes free embeddings and is not a generalization guarantee, so it cannot establish that pixel encoders learn or transfer the geometry.
Reviewer-identified premise gap: no experiment retrains heads over all valid supports to measure the theorem's exact Stability condition.
failure_modes: A representation can generalize accurately while calibrated posterior values vary across supports, placing it outside the theorem despite practical success.
A low-dimensional affine hull permits different ambient-space probe weights with identical predictions on all realized embeddings, breaking parameter identification.
Probe-span projection can discard non-additive embedding information and make additive reconstruction appear more complete than in the full representation.
Checkpoint-level correlation can arise because better pretrained models improve both factor decoding and accuracy, with geometry acting as an effect or proxy rather than a cause.
Random high-dimensional, centered factor estimates can look nearly orthogonal without semantic modularity.
Selecting probe hyperparameters on reported test performance can inflate both the downstream score and its association with the representation metric.
Directly optimized tuple embeddings can satisfy the proposed geometry even when an encoder trained from pixels would exploit entangled shortcuts.
reusable_insights: Separate necessity for an operational success metric from necessity under an added invariance axiom; state both prominently.
When functional equality is observed only on a data manifold, identify linear parameters on its affine hull or explicitly assume full affine span.
Max-margin directional convergence should not be combined with calibrated-posterior claims without a scale convention or regularized finite optimum.
A causal geometry test should rotate, remove, or orthogonalize identified factor subspaces while matching margins and full-grid in-distribution accuracy.
Representation metrics based on label-informed projection need full-space and cross-fitted variants to reveal transductive coupling.
A genuine encoder-level composition test must verify that held-out combinations have zero training mass, not merely hold them out from a downstream probe.
open_questions: Can Proposition 1 be repaired by restricting all readouts to aff(f(X)) and proving the more-than-half branch without invalid cross supports?
What approximate factorization and orthogonality bounds follow from epsilon-transfer and distributional, rather than exact, Stability?
Does cross-fitted full-space geometry predict held-out combinations after controlling for model family, dimension, pretraining scale, and linear separability?
Do causal orthogonalization or factor-subspace ablations change compositional accuracy while preserving ordinary concept accuracy and margins?
Will encoders trained from scratch on verified factorial supports converge to the same geometry across natural images, language, and generative models?

competitive_landscape.title: Does Data Scaling Lead to Visual Compositional Generalization?
competitive_landscape.difference: Uselis et al. measure whether scaling datasets and models yields systematic recombination and report persistent gaps. The present paper seeks a representation-level necessary condition rather than another scaling curve, but its frozen-encoder experiments inherit the same exposure and split concerns.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Generalization from First Principles
competitive_landscape.difference: Wiedemer et al. derive data-support and model conditions for extrapolating a compositional data-generating process. Their guarantee does not impose exact posterior invariance across all retrained heads or orthogonal factors, so it is a competing formalization of what composition requires.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Risk Minimization
competitive_landscape.difference: CRM studies minimal diverse supports and an objective for full Cartesian generalization. It supplies the cross-like support motivation used here, while the current result adds a claimed necessary embedding geometry under a particular downstream learning rule.

competitive_landscape.title: Linear Spaces of Meanings: Compositional Structures in Vision-Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Trager et al. model VLM embeddings as combinations of a smaller basis of ideal-word vectors and evaluate linear operations in CLIP. The present paper adds a conditional necessity result, but additive VLM factor structure itself is prior art.

competitive_landscape.title: Deciphering the Role of Representation Disentanglement: Investigating Compositional Generalization in CLIP Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Abbasi et al. empirically study how disentanglement and sparsity relate to unusual visual compositions. That work tests representation properties without claiming exact orthogonality is universally necessary; it is closer to the present empirical question than the theorem's idealized setup.

competitive_landscape.title: When does compositional structure yield compositional generalization? A kernel theory
competitive_landscape.difference: This kernel analysis links compositional transfer to architectural inductive biases and training dynamics without making additive orthogonal embeddings the primitive cause. It is an alternative mechanism class the checkpoint correlations do not distinguish.

competitive_landscape.title: When and How Does CLIP Enable Domain and Compositional Generalization?
competitive_landscape.difference: This work probes atomic visual knowledge and systematic recombination in CLIP-like models, providing task-level evidence complementary to the present factor-geometry metrics. It underscores that linear decodability alone need not imply robust compositional behavior.

competitive_landscape.title: Visual Representation Learning Does Not Generalize Strongly Within the Same Domain
competitive_landscape.difference: Schott et al. train more than 2,000 models on recombination, interpolation, and extrapolation splits of factorized visual datasets and find weak within-domain generalization. It is direct priority for the datasets and the distinction between factor decodability and learning the underlying mechanism.

competitive_landscape.title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis and the Geometry of Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This linear-representation analysis develops geometric criteria and empirical tests for concept directions. It predates the present use of additive factors and highlights that a task-correlated linear geometry is weaker than a necessity or causal result.

competitive_landscape.title: Enhancing Compositional Generalization via Compositional Feature Alignment
competitive_landscape.difference: CFA uses compositional feature alignment and orthogonalized linear heads to improve vision-language composition. It is direct priority for making factor separation an intervention; the present paper differs by claiming conditional necessity and primarily observing frozen encoders.

competitive_landscape.title: Are Object-Centric Representations Better At Compositional Generalization?
competitive_landscape.difference: This concurrent work compares object-centric and dense representations under controlled data diversity, downstream capacity, and compute, finding conditional object-centric advantages rather than a universal necessity. It is a key discriminator for whether orthogonal additive directions are cause, correlate, or one realization among several.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first derivation of linear additive and cross-concept orthogonal representation structure as a necessary consequence of compositional generalization under standard downstream training, plus broad evidence that current vision embeddings partially approach that geometry.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Propositions 1-4 connect exact desiderata to binary max-margin geometry, and Sections 5/H measure additive R-squared, factor cosines, and dimensionality across multiple encoder families and synthetic objectives.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The conditional theorem framing and broad diagnostic sweep are novel and useful, but the strongest necessity wording overreaches ordinary compositional generalization. Two proof bridges are missing as written, the empirical metric is correlational and label-informed, and prior work already studies compositional supports, linear representation geometry, disentanglement, and orthogonalized feature alignment.

Audit result: held-out composition occurs only at downstream probe training, not verified encoder pretraining; there is no exact Stability measurement or leakage audit; architecture, dimension, data, and pretraining compute are unmatched across checkpoints; projected-whitened R-squared is a descriptive, label-informed/transductive association rather than causal evidence; main correlations lack coefficients and main-panel uncertainty; theorem-to-natural-model and binary-to-multivalued transfer are unestablished. Author-stated limitations are the idealized exact Stability premise, the fixed-encoder/single-dataset mismatch, and the non-guarantee of the synthetic study; the affine-domain, support-family, split-language, and GD-calibration defects are reviewer contradiction audits.
